checkpoint.q: Four properties of the Batch API
checkpoint.a: It costs 50% of standard prices on input and output. It is asynchronous: most batches finish within an hour, and requests still unprocessed after 24 hours expire. It does not stream (stream: true is rejected), and results come back in any order, available for 29 days.

checkpoint.q: What is the only safe join key?
checkpoint.a: custom_id. The docs state that results can be returned in any order, so joining by position can attach answers to the wrong inputs without any error. Give every request a unique custom_id that maps back to your source record.

checkpoint.q: Does batch stack with caching? At what discount?
checkpoint.a: Yes. The pricing page says caching multipliers stack with the Batch API discount, so a cache read inside a batch costs 0.1 x 0.5 = 0.05x the standard input price, and a 5-minute cache write costs 1.25 x 0.5 = 0.625x. Because a batch can take longer than five minutes, the docs suggest the 1-hour cache TTL for shared context in batches.
